solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nothing right about disgusting feeder

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the two short pieces before it are read backwards

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
RT is a standard abbreviation for right, as in Rt Hon
ugh is the exclamation of someone disgusted

explanation.surface: A revolting eating trough, with nothing right about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the two short pieces round; RT is a standard abbreviation for right, as in Rt Hon.
explanation.definitionFit: A trough is the long open container from which farm animals feed, so it is a feeder.

clue.text: Very violent pull, needing energy to operate bell

parts.note: to tow is to pull along
E is the physics symbol for energy
to ring a bell is to operate it

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer needs energy for a hefty pull on the rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A towering rage is an extreme, intense one, so towering means very violent.

clue.text: Result of a number of voters switching?

indicators.note: switching means the two halves of the word trade places

parts.note: turnout is the number of people who vote

explanation.surface: An election result caused by voters changing sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching' swaps the halves of TURNOUT so OUT comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Outturn is the quantity produced or the actual outcome, a synonym of result.

clue.text: Barrier, and two other elements of train journey

parts.words: two other elements of train journey
parts.note: a train has a guard on board and runs on a rail, two parts of any train journey

explanation.surface: A barrier alongside other features of a trip by train.
explanation.walkthrough: The two parts, a guard and a rail, combine into the barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardrail is a protective rail along a road edge or drop, a kind of barrier.

clue.text: Weapon criminal holds level

indicators.note: holds means the word for criminal keeps the weapon inside it

parts.note: criminal, as in a bad lot, gives BAD
a lance is a long spear carried by knights

explanation.surface: An armed criminal keeps a cool, level head.
explanation.definitionFit: Something balanced is even, with neither side higher, which is what level means as an adjective.

clue.text: Not unusual to be exhausted by a full shift

parts.note: all in is slang for exhausted
a day's work is a full shift on the job

explanation.surface: A worker worn out by a long shift.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something routine and expected, part of the normal job.

clue.text: Special terms in old ship announced

indicators.note: announced means the ship's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth

explanation.surface: Nautical jargon used on an old ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the special jargon or slang of a particular group.

clue.text: Brutish islander, defence finally failing, jailed?

indicators.note: the question mark tells the solver to read jailed literally, as shut inside the prison word

parts.note: to be jailed is to be put in the can, slang for prison

indicators.note: finally failing means the last letter is lost

parts.note: an alibi is a defence in court, proof of being elsewhere

explanation.surface: A savage islander, his defence collapsing at the end, is locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jailed' works twice: it names the CAN, slang for prison, and also says to put the shortened defence inside it, so the container has no separate signal word.
explanation.definitionFit: Caliban is the savage, monstrous native of the island in Shakespeare's play The Tempest.

clue.text: One taking steps and collapsing on ground, getting up

indicators.note: on means the first piece sits on top of the second in a down answer
collapsing means the three letters of the little word fall into a new order
getting up means the word reads upwards in this down clue

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a public playing field in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone stepping out and then collapsing on the ground before getting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsing' makes DAN from AND; 'getting up' reverses REC to CER. A REC is a British recreation ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A dancer moves by taking dance steps, so is one taking steps.

clue.text: Light reading for one trip thrown in case?

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters go inside the legal case word

parts.note: an action is a case in law

indicators.note: thrown means these letters are tossed about into a new order

parts.note: the words for and trip are taken as written, with one as the Roman numeral I between them

explanation.surface: An easy novel for a journey, tossed into a suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like luggage but is a lawsuit, an ACTION; the shuffled letters sit after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the genre of easy, undemanding bestsellers sold to travellers waiting for flights.

clue.text: Heartily sick after leave, rejecting doctor

indicators.note: after means the word for sick comes at the end
rejecting means the doctor's abbreviation is thrown out of the word for leave

parts.note: to leave a place is to withdraw from it
sick means ill

explanation.surface: Someone off sick after taking leave refuses to see the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' leaves WITHAW; 'after' sets the sick word at the end. 'leave' looks like a holiday but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something with a will is to do it energetically and wholeheartedly, which is heartily.

clue.text: In depression, find a physician

indicators.note: In places the letter from the clue's 'a' inside the word for depression

parts.note: a glen is a narrow valley, a depression in the land

explanation.surface: A doctor called in to treat someone's depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' reads as low mood but means a valley here.
explanation.definitionFit: Galen was the famous Greek physician of the second century whose medical teaching dominated for centuries.

clue.text: Gather work engrosses old politicians

indicators.note: engrosses means the word for work takes in the abbreviation for old

parts.note: to run a machine is to work it
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A job absorbing veteran politicians collects them together.
explanation.definitionFit: To round up people or animals is to bring them together, a phrasal synonym of gather.

clue.text: Remarkable why restaurant turns one away?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, the phrase is the excuse a full restaurant gives a diner without a booking

explanation.surface: Wondering at the strange reason a restaurant refuses a customer.
explanation.definitionFit: Notable means worth noticing, striking, which matches remarkable as a synonym.

clue.text: Assassin arrested by Lenin jailed

indicators.note: arrested by means the answer is held captive inside the following words

explanation.surface: A killer seized by the Soviet leader and imprisoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja was a Japanese warrior trained in stealth, espionage and covert killing.

clue.text: Newly interpret old advice: great

parts.note: rede is an archaic word for advice or counsel
fine means excellent, great

explanation.surface: Giving fresh meaning to some old advice that turns out great.
explanation.walkthrough: REDE is archaic English for counsel, as in Hamlet's 'recks not his own rede'.
explanation.definitionFit: To redefine something is to set out its meaning again in a new way, so to interpret it newly.

clue.text: Intended to raise a tree metres higher in the sky

indicators.note: higher means these pieces sit above the rest in a down answer

parts.note: a fir is a coniferous tree
M is the abbreviation for metres

indicators.note: to raise means the letter named by the clue's 'a' moves up to the top of the word

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: Planting a tree so that it reaches metres up into the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to raise a' lifts the A of MEANT to the top, making AMENT; FIR + M go 'higher' still.
explanation.definitionFit: The firmament is a poetic word for the heavens, the vault of the sky.

clue.text: Predictable finale from Jack, born fool

indicators.note: finale from means take only the last letter of the name

parts.note: née marks a maiden name, meaning born
a jerk is a stupid person

explanation.surface: The predictable ending for Jack, a natural-born fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A knee-jerk reaction is automatic and unthinking, so wholly predictable.

clue.text: Slender cook with fat children

parts.note: slender, as in a slender chance, means small
to fry is to cook in hot fat

explanation.surface: A thin chef frying with fat to feed the kids.
explanation.definitionFit: Small fry is an informal plural term for young children, or anyone insignificant.

clue.text: In revolutionary day, I sounded like a queen?

indicators.note: In means the single letter I is set inside the revolutionary's name

parts.note: Mao Zedong led the Chinese communist revolution
WED is the abbreviation for Wednesday

explanation.surface: On a day of revolution, someone speaking like a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queen' suggests royalty, but a queen is also a female cat, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen is a female cat, so one sounding like a queen made a cat's cry.

clue.text: Closely examining wingless bird

indicators.note: wingless means the word loses its two outside letters, its wings

parts.note: probing means examining closely

explanation.surface: Examining a bird that has lost its wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wingless' strips the outer letters P and G from PROBING.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is a small red-breasted songbird familiar in British gardens.

clue.text: Ask for poem, say, and muck it up

parts.note: to beg is to ask for something earnestly
a rime is a poem, as in The Rime of the Ancient Mariner; say marks an example

explanation.surface: Requesting a poem, then making a mess of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrime something is to make it dirty, to cover it with grime or muck.

clue.text: Travels up to collect bill for salt

indicators.note: to collect means the reversed word gathers the bill inside it
up means the word reads upwards in this down clue

parts.note: goes means travels
an ad, or advertisement, is a bill posted up

explanation.surface: Someone travels to pick up a bill for salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses GOES to SEOG, which collects AD. 'salt' is an old sailor, not the seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is an experienced sailor, and so is a sea dog.

clue.text: Bouncy castle I played with

indicators.note: played with means these letters are toyed with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A child on a bouncy castle: 'I played with it.'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncy castle' reads as one thing, but 'Bouncy' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic material springs back after stretching, so it is resilient and bouncy.

clue.text: Worker going up the wall perhaps left during row

definitions.text: Worker going up the wall perhaps

indicators.note: during means the abbreviation for left comes within the row word

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A worker driven up the wall by a row with a colleague who left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up the wall' suggests losing one's temper; a tiler literally works up a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiler fixes tiles, often moving up a wall as the courses rise, so is such a worker.

clue.text: Argue with one interpretation of ninety degrees?

parts.note: ninety degrees is a right angle, written with R for right as R ANGLE

explanation.surface: Disputing how to read a figure of ninety degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrangle is to dispute noisily or at length, a synonym of argue.

clue.text: Peg leg almost put back on Jones's partner

indicators.note: on means the reversed piece is attached after the partner's name

parts.note: Dow and Jones founded the Dow Jones index, so Jones's partner is Dow

indicators.note: put back means the shortened word is reversed
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the word leg is taken as written before shortening

explanation.surface: Someone with a wooden peg leg, nearly fixed back on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims LEG to LE, 'put back' turns that into EL, and it goes 'on' DOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowel is a headless wooden pin or peg used to join pieces of wood.

clue.text: Leading a chosen group, one senior member of it?

definitions.text: Leading a chosen group, one senior member of it?

indicators.note: Leading means the first pieces come before the rest

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
an elite is a select or chosen group

explanation.surface: Describing a leader of a select band who belongs to it.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes a member of the biblical Chosen People; 'Leading' puts the first two pieces before the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Israelites are the biblical Chosen People, so one of them is a member of that chosen group.

clue.text: Panicking disastrously as a grenade exploded

indicators.note: exploded means the letters are blown apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Troops panic badly when a grenade goes off.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Gospels the Gadarene swine, possessed by demons, rushed headlong into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Gadarene describes a headlong rush to disaster, after the biblical herd of pigs.

clue.text: Vein runs through meat

indicators.note: through means the runs abbreviation passes inside the meat

parts.note: steak is a cut of meat
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A line of fat running through a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A streak is a thin line or band of a different colour, as is a vein in marble or meat.
